subject: Equinox evaluation: ops & latency validation plan

messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Equinox discovery — post-call recap and technical asks

Hi team,

Quick recap from this morning's call with Olivia / Equinox ML Ops: they run an internal LLM-driven assistant across customer support and internal search. Main asks: predictable p95/p99 latency under production concurrency, clear throughput (tokens/sec) at different batch sizes, and a simple test harness they can run alongside their hyperscaler tests for apples-to-apples comparisons.

Key constraints and asks from Equinox:
- Target 100 QPS burst, steady-state 25–40 QPS.
- Common prompt lengths ≈ 256 tokens; worst-case sequences up to 1024 tokens.
- Need p95 < 150ms for short (<=256) generation and p99 < 400ms for longer sequences, if possible.
- Concerned about cold-starts during autoscale and model-quantization quality regressions.

Next steps I committed to:
1) Share an ops-focused benchmark plan (matrix, metrics, data capture).
2) Propose a short A/B test matrix that Equinox can run against hyperscaler endpoints and our hosted endpoints (we'll also run mirrored tests).
3) Draft an SOW/neutral test agreement and a small trial uplift credit.

I've attached my raw discovery notes and a first-pass benchmark-plan spreadsheet. Marissa — can you own the test matrix and the exact metric definitions (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cold vs warm, batch sizes)? Connor — can you prep a lightweight harness (curl + python client) that captures timing headers and KV cache hit metrics? Stephanie — I need a recommended commercial treatment (trial credit + simple commercial terms) and anything we should pre-clear with Legal.

Thanks — Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Equinox discovery — post-call recap and technical asks

Thanks Rishi — I pulled the sheet and sketched a concrete test matrix. High-level proposal (will update the spreadsheet):

Test matrix (mirrored across Redwood hosted, Redwood-dedicated, and Hyperscaler-A):
- Prompt classes: short (<=256), medium (257–512), long (513–1024)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16 (and a raw streaming mode for token-by-token latency)
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 5, 20, 50 concurrent clients (emulate 25–100 QPS ranges)
- Warm vs cold: measure 1st request after model spin-up, then steady-state after 30s of continuous traffic
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (generation complete), median token-step latency, tokens/sec (aggregate and per-worker), CPU/GPU utilization, KV-cache hit ratio, memory footprint, and failure/timeout rates

Data capture notes: include raw per-request traces with timestamps (client_send, server_receive, model_infer_start, model_infer_end, server_send). We'll bake trace keys into the harness so Equinox can post results to our shared Drive folder.

On quantization: include a small quality checklist — BLEU/ROUGE/Perplexity not ideal for generative assistant; instead use a prompt-set of 50 representative prompts (we'll ask Equinox to mark 10 high-sensitivity prompts). We'll run 8-bit and 4-bit variants to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Connor — here's the schema I want from your harness so we can generate identical CSVs: request_id, prompt_class, batch_size, concurrency, seq_len, token_count, start_ts, infer_start_ts, infer_end_ts, end_ts, p50/p95/p99 placeholders, tokens_per_sec, worker_id, kv_cache_hit (bool), error_code. Keep it simple.

I'll update the spreadsheet with explicit rows and sample charts (p95 vs concurrency, tokens/sec vs batch).

- Marissa
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Equinox discovery — post-call recap and technical asks

I started a lightweight harness repo (internal gist link in Drive). Notes for the team:
- I'll provide a Python runner that can target (a) Redwood hosted API key, (b) Redwood Dedicated endpoint, (c) external Hyperscaler endpoints (they supply API details).
- Default concurrency driver will use gevent-based clients to minimize client-side jitter.
- I'll emit both CSVs and Jaeger-compatible traces (span names: client_send, server_receive, model_forward, server_send).
- For KV cache metrics, we'll surface a simple header in responses: X-Redwood-KV-Hit: true|false and include it in the trace. If Hyperscaler can't provide KV flags, we'll at least record latency deltas for repeated prefixes to infer caching behavior.

ETA: initial harness + example run by Thu EOD (2027-08-05). Will link results to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_benchmark_plan

- Connor
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Thanks — this looks great. Quick commercial/ops notes from my side:
- I'll propose a 30-day evaluation with a $15k trial credit focused on inference units; covers hosted usage + Dedicated trial capacity for 2 weeks if they want to validate autoscale behaviors.
- I'll attach SOW-draft-v0.1 and a short neutral test agreement for legal review (I copied legal@equinox.ai on the outbound when we send the docs).
- Ask: if we run Dedicated-side tests, we should provide an engineer-hours allowance (4hrs) to instrument KV-caching metrics and help them interpret p95/p99 regressions. I'll propose that in the SOW.

One more thing — pricing note for the data room: if quantized 4-bit models demonstrate parity on high-sensitivity prompts, we should propose a 20% discounted rate for quantized inference in the trial and capture that as a negotiable line item.

I'll coordinate the legal thread and send out the SOW by Thu morning.

- Stephanie

Thanks for the clear plan and quick turnaround.

We reviewed the proposed matrix internally — that's exactly the kind of reproducible framework we need. A few clarifications from our side before we run the tests:
- We'll provide a fixed set of 50 prompts and flag 10 high-sensitivity prompts as Marissa suggested.
- For Hyperscaler comparisons, we prefer Hyperscaler-A and Hyperscaler-B endpoints; Samir (cc'd) will help run an independent baseline.
- We need the harness to produce per-request traces and an aggregated JSON summary (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, failures) so we can attach results to our procurement packet.
- Timeline: we'll start mirrored runs next Tue (2027-08-10). Can you confirm you'll have the harness and initial Redwood-hosted results by Mon EOD (2027-08-09)?

If we see a clear latency advantage at p95/p99 and acceptable quality for quantized models on the high-sensitivity prompts, we'll move to a pilot (goal: production by Q4). Also — please include a short note about SLAs you can commit to during the trial.

Looking forward,
Olivia
